subject: math
cluster: Solve real-life and mathematical problems using numerical and algebraic expressions and equations
skillName: Equations and Inequalities from Word Problems
intro: Each problem describes a real-life situation. Define a variable for the unknown, write a two-step equation or inequality, solve it, and interpret your answer in context. All coefficients are positive integers and all solutions are positive integers.

items.prompt: A gym charges a $\$25$ sign-up fee plus $\$15$ per month. Lena paid $\$115$ in all. Write and solve the equation $15m + 25 = 115$ to find the number of months $m$ she paid for.
The perimeter of a rectangle is $54$ cm. Its length is $15$ cm, so $2w + 30 = 54$, where $w$ is the width. Write and solve the equation to find the width $w$.
A taxi charges a $\$4$ base fare plus $\$3$ per mile. The total ride cost $\$28$. Solve $3m + 4 = 28$ to find the number of miles $m$.
Marcus is saving for a bike. He already has $\$40$ and adds $\$12$ each week. He needs $\$160$ total. Solve $12w + 40 = 160$ to find the number of weeks $w$.
A printing shop charges a $\$10$ setup fee plus $\$2$ per shirt. An order cost $\$50$. Solve $2s + 10 = 50$ to find the number of shirts $s$.
Tickets to a fair cost $\$5$ each, plus a $\$7$ parking fee. A family spent $\$42$ in all. Solve $5t + 7 = 42$ to find the number of tickets $t$.
A plumber charges a $\$60$ visit fee plus $\$45$ per hour. A bill was $\$240$. Solve $45h + 60 = 240$ to find the number of hours $h$ worked.
Sara has $\$100$ to spend. Each book costs $\$8$. She can spend at most $\$100$, so $8b \le 100$. Solve the inequality to find the greatest number of whole books $b$ she can buy.

steps: Since $b$ must be a whole number of books, the greatest value is $12$.
Sara can buy at most $12$ books.

items.prompt: A vending machine has a $\$1$ service fee plus $\$2$ per drink. You have at most $\$15$, so $2d + 1 \le 15$. Solve to find the greatest number of drinks $d$ you can buy.

steps: You can buy at most $7$ drinks.

items.prompt: A pizza party costs $\$20$ for delivery plus $\$9$ per pizza. The budget is at most $\$110$, so $9p + 20 \le 110$. Solve to find the greatest number of pizzas $p$ that can be ordered.

steps: At most $10$ pizzas can be ordered.

items.prompt: Jordan needs to read at least $90$ pages. He has already read $30$ pages and reads $20$ pages per day, so $20d + 30 \ge 90$. Solve to find the least number of days $d$ he needs.
A phone plan costs $\$30$ per month plus a one-time $\$50$ activation fee. The total paid was $\$200$. Solve $30m + 50 = 200$ to find the number of months $m$.

steps: The plan was paid for $5$ months.

items.prompt: A bakery sells muffins for $\$3$ each plus a $\$6$ box fee. A customer paid $\$36$. Solve $3n + 6 = 36$ to find the number of muffins $n$.
A bus tour charges $\$8$ per person plus a $\$16$ guide fee. A group paid $\$96$. Solve $8x + 16 = 96$ to find the number of people $x$.

steps: There were $10$ people in the group.

items.prompt: An online store charges $\$7$ per item plus $\$5$ shipping. The order total was $\$54$. Solve $7k + 5 = 54$ to find the number of items $k$.
